scope: Actual authenticated HTTP PUT of the same governed entity in 150001 entities and 300000 relations

before.label: before
before.workload: one governed record revision through real authenticated HTTP; no unrelated pytest or browser workload

after.label: after
after.workload: one governed record revision through real authenticated HTTP; no unrelated pytest or browser workload

conditions: No concurrent pytest or unrelated browser was running during either PUT.
The before encoder was warm from the preceding real product run; the after encoder had two explicit warmups, reported separately.
The entity revision increased from r2 to r3 before optimization, and r3 to r4 afterward. Entity and relation counts stayed fixed.
Other desktop applications and background storage/index maintenance were not stopped. This is one observational pair, not a latency percentile or a universal speedup.
changes: Reuse one detached authority planning snapshot for service validation and FormalFactWriter.prepare.
Remove redundant full-snapshot JSON roundtrip and planner deepcopy; use copy-on-write for changed rows and inherited source metadata.
Keep a fresh complete execution snapshot, canonical SHA256 fingerprint, dependencies, transaction and table-lock guards.

verification.focused_independent_review: No unresolved P1/P2 after the inherited-source-metadata regression was fixed.

remaining_limit: Ordinary formal writes still take full project planning and fresh execution snapshots. The measured 125.454 seconds remains slow; bounded formal planning and an equally strong authority proof need separate design and validation.
